ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A poll identifies the proportions of high-income and low-income voters who support a decrease in taxes. If we need to know the answer to be within ±0.02 at the 95% confidence interval, what sample size should be taken?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The inequality given in the image is σ_d ≤ (0.5√2)/√n, and 1.96σ_d ≤ 0.02. Then reason: The problem is comparing the proportions of voters who support tax cuts among the two categories of high-income and low-income voters, so the upper bound of the standard error of the difference between two proportions is used. To make the error of the 95% confidence interval within ±0.02, it is necessary to satisfy 1.96σ_d ≤ 0.02. Substituting the upper bound σ_d ≤ (0.5√2)/√n given in the image gives 1.96(0.5√2/√n) ≤ 0.02. Rearranging gives √n ≥ (1.96·0.5√2)/0.02. Squaring both sides: n ≥ [(1.96·0.5√2)/0.02]^2 ≈ 4802. Taking an upward conservative integer according to the required sample size, the sample size should be 4803.

method.method_draft: Treat the problem as planning a poll to estimate the difference between two independent proportions: high-income support proportion minus low-income support proportion. From the text, read the desired error bound E = 0.02 and confidence level 95%, giving z = 1.96. Since no prior proportions are given, use the conservative maximum Bernoulli variance p(1-p) ≤ 0.25 for each group. For equal sample size n in each group, the standard error of the difference is at most √(0.25/n + 0.25/n) = √(0.5/n). Require 1.96√(0.5/n) ≤ 0.02. Squaring gives n ≥ 1.96²·0.5/0.02² ≈ 4802, so select 4803 to ensure the required accuracy.
